evidence: gpt-oss-120b uses "order vertices by degree descending to improve pruning" and bitmask vertex sets; the other attempts enumerate "independent sets" or candidate subsets
affordance_in_statement: The net polarity of a link is calculated by adding the polarities of its two coupled nodes, where a positive polarity evaluates to +1 and a negative polarity evaluates to -1. If the net polarity of any resonant link is strictly greater than zero, the trap will destabilize and fail.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal: the condition is intrinsically equivalent to requiring the selected vertices to be an independent set. It can only be re-presented indirectly, for example by defining safety as a global equilibrium predicate rather than explicitly exposing the forbidden pairwise condition.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that no linked pair may both be selected and solves the resulting independent-set feasibility problem with degree ordering, bitmasks, and pruning.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: If the net polarity of any resonant link is strictly greater than zero, the trap will destabilize and fail.

common_affordance: The link constraint is exactly the independent-set condition: both endpoints of every resonant link cannot be among the k positive nodes.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its meet-in-the-middle implementation enumerates too many half-graph masks and performs excessive per-mask compatibility work, causing TLE near n=46.
It tries every k-subset using combinations, which is infeasible for n=46 and middle-sized k.
It imports numpy in the submission environment and terminates with a runtime error before solving.

recommended_edit: No reliable task-preserving edit can defeat the surviving solver: the independent-set structure is the core mathematical task. If presentation must be changed, hide the reduction by describing safety only through an equivalent global equilibrium predicate, while recognizing that this is merely obfuscation and not a robust difficulty increase.
regression_risk: An equivalent re-presentation could make the defeated brute-force models recognize the independent-set formulation more clearly, potentially worsening their performance only by making their existing approach easier to apply.
